name: E-Government administrative intranet regional data center/support node
developer: Government of Senegal / Huawei Technologies / China Machinery Engineering Corporation
notes: AidData's Senegal e-government project record says Phase 1 laid fiber in Dakar, Thies, Louga, Saint Louis, Diourbel, Kaolack and Fatick and created data centers to support the administrative intranet. It also says the fixed/IP/mobile telephony network covered 11 regional capitals including Diourbel. The record does not identify a separately named Diourbel facility, so this is weak aggregate evidence.

name: PAIX Dakar / DKR-1
notes: PAIX announced construction of a Dakar facility in Les Mamelles/Ouakam, with 918 sqm of white space and 1.2MW of critical power, expected operational in 2026. Data Center Map lists the site as under construction with site code DKR-1 and the same 1.2MW power figure.

name: Onix Data Centre Senegal
developer: Onix Data Centres Ltd. / La Colombe Group
notes: DCD reported Onix launched colocation in Dakar on February 16, 2023 at the 2Africa cable landing station, with access to ACE, MainOne and 2Africa. Public specifications were not shared; Data Center Map lists the facility within the 2Africa Cable Landing Station in Almadies.

name: Diamniadio National Datacenter
developer: Sénégal Numérique S.A. / ADIE, with Huawei support
notes: President Macky Sall commissioned the Diamniadio National Datacenter in June 2021 at the Digital Technology Park. DCD reported it would host state data and applications, had 500 sqm hosting capacity, was managed by ADIE, and was financed by a Chinese loan with Huawei support. AidData also links Phase 3 of the e-government project to construction of a 4x400 sqm data center in Diamniadio.

name: Sonatel Rufisque Data Center
notes: Data Center Map lists Sonatel's Rufisque Data Center on Route de Rufisque, with Tier 3 and ISO27001 labels and a second-room expansion. Uptime Institute's Senegal awards page is included as a primary certification reference, but the public listing was not fully retrievable during this pass; no public MW figure was found.

name: Yas Diamniadio Data Center
developer: Yas / Axian Telecom, formerly Free Senegal / Tigo Senegal
notes: Data Center Map lists a Tier 3 Yas Diamniadio Data Center at QR27+VPX in Rufisque/Diamniadio. The listing says the facility was originally developed by SenConnect for Tigo, later Free Senegal, and rebranded as Yas after Axian Telecom's 2024 ownership change. No public MW figure was found.

name: Free Data Center Diamniadio
notes: Data Center Map lists Free Data Center Diamniadio within Diamniadio, describing data hosting and backup services and Tier III design/facility positioning. This may overlap historically or commercially with the Free/Yas Diamniadio footprint, so it is retained as an aggregate-listed facility with weak evidence.

name: STELLARIX Senegal
notes: Data Center Map lists STELLARIX Senegal within Sangalkam/Diamniadio. Public source detail is sparse; Africa Tech Festival's STELLARIX profile describes the operator as developing African data center facilities, but no capacity or firm operating status for Senegal was confirmed.

name: N+One Senegal Digital Technology Park data centers
developer: N+One Datacenters / Ministry of Digital Economy and Telecommunications / DER/FJ / Senegal Digital Technology Park
notes: DCD reported N+One would build three data centers in Dakar as part of a partnership tied to Senegal's Digital Technology Park and the Digital Senegal plan. Specifications were not shared, and no later public completion evidence was found in this pass, so status remains announced.

name: WHO Dakar Emergencies Hub resilient data center
notes: A July 2026 DevelopmentAid tender notice sought implementation of a resilient data center to strengthen WHO's Dakar emergency/intelligence hub. This appears to be an institutional IT/data-room project rather than a commercial colocation or hyperscale facility; no capacity was disclosed.
